task: Audacity is open with an empty project. First, change the Project Rate to 48000 Hz. Generate a linear chirp with these exact settings: Waveform = Sine, Start frequency = 200 Hz, End frequency = 4000 Hz, Start amplitude = 0.8, End amplitude = 0.8, Interpolation = Linear, Duration = 4.0 seconds. Then append 2.0 seconds of silence after the chirp. The total track length should be 6.0 seconds. task_grounding:
Audacity is open with an empty project.

First, change the Project Rate (in the lower-left of the Audacity window, or via Tracks > Resample) to 48000 Hz so any generated audio uses a 48 kHz sample rate.

Then use Generate > Chirp... to generate a linear chirp with these exact settings: Waveform = Sine, Start frequency = 200 Hz, End frequency = 4000 Hz, Start amplitude = 0.8, End amplitude = 0.8, Interpolation = Linear, Duration = 4.0 seconds. Click OK.

Place the cursor at the end of the chirp (position 4.0 seconds) and use Generate > Silence... to append 2.0 seconds of silence after the chirp. The total track length should now be 6.0 seconds.

Export the full track to /home/user/Music/chirp_silence.wav using File > Export > Export as WAV... with 'WAV (Microsoft) signed 16-bit PCM' at 48000 Hz mono. Accept any metadata dialog defaults.

verification.description: First 4s has signal (chirp RMS roughly -3 to -5 dB for amp 0.8)
